_meta.purpose: Documented travel-related importations of an orthoebolavirus disease into a country without ongoing transmission, 2000 to 5 October 2026, with whether locally acquired confirmed cases followed. It prices Block 11's Kenya question and is updated with that question's outcome after resolution.
_meta.inclusion_rules: Unit = one destination-country importation episode: the first travel-related, laboratory-confirmed orthoebolavirus case (EBOV, SUDV, BDBV, TAFV) detected in a country with no ongoing transmission, 2000-01-01 to 2026-10-05. Multiple imported cases in the same country in the same episode = one unit; a new unit starts only after the previous episode in that country had ended (no transmission / end declared). The index person travelled while infected (incubating or symptomatic; commercial or private; road or air) and was diagnosed after arrival. EXCLUDED: planned medical evacuations of known/suspected cases, laboratory accidents, needle-stick exposures in the outbreak country, cases diagnosed only after returning to the origin country, and episodes whose imported index was never laboratory-confirmed (reported separately as sensitivity cases). Outcome YES = >=1 laboratory-confirmed case acquired in the destination country attributed to that episode; NO = none reported after 21/42-day follow-up. Kenya October 2026 excluded (forecast target). Applied mechanically; every judgement is recorded in notes, excluded[] and uncertainties[]. Sources restricted to WHO (DON, statements, AFRO, WER, situation reports), US CDC MMWR/EID, ECDC, national ministries, and peer-reviewed papers.
sensitivity: the registered class, concurrent arrivals merged: 6 of 12 (0.500)
the research's separate-units coding (New York and Kayes as their own NO units, Bamako excluded): 5 of 13 (0.393)
registered class without the two Liberian episodes whose YES rests on reading WHO wording: 4 of 10 (0.409)
indexes who were returning responders or health workers (Glasgow, Sardinia, Paris): 0 of 3; other travellers: 6 of 9
_meta.unit_rule_applied: The research brief, written before the search (2026-10-06T23:09Z), defined the unit as one destination-country importation episode and said that several imported cases arriving in the same country in the same episode are one unit. The search added a boundary clause (a new unit starts only after the previous episode in that country has ended), which points the same way, but coded two concurrent arrivals as separate units: New York 2014 beside Dallas, and Kayes beside the Bamako cluster in Mali. The registered class applies the brief's rule literally and merges both, giving 6 of 12 episodes with local transmission. The separate-units coding (5 of 13) is reported as a sensitivity.

episodes.date_precision: arrival unknown (March 2014); confirmation: first 2 lab-confirmed cases reported by MOHSW for 14-30 March 2014 (WHO DON 1 Apr 2014); exact lab date not stated
episodes.travel_mode: unknown (cross-border from Guinea into Lofa County; mode not stated)
episodes.notes: MMWR (Nyenswah 2014): 'In March 2014, Ebola virus infection was detected in Lofa County in a patient returning from an outbreak area in Guinea.' WHO DON 27 Mar 2014: Liberia's suspected cases had travel histories to Gueckedou. By 11 Apr 2014 WHO reported 6 lab-confirmed cases in Liberia, all fatal, 'this includes 3 HCW'. JUDGEMENT: the 3 lab-confirmed health-care workers are counted as locally acquired (infected while caring for patients in Liberia); WHO does not state their place of infection explicitly, so 3 is an inferred lower bound. Caveat: this importation happened as the Guinea outbreak was only being recognised (declared 21-23 Mar 2014); it is not analogous to an importation into a prepared country. Whether Liberia's June 2014 resurgence descends from this importation is not established and is NOT used for the outcome.

episodes.notes: Liberia had ended its previous flare on 14 Jan 2016 (no ongoing transmission). 30-year-old wife of a man who died in Macenta (Koropara/Macenta cluster) travelled to Monrovia with her children, developed symptoms there, died 31 Mar; post-mortem confirmation 1 Apr. Two sons (5 and 2 years) confirmed 1-5 April. JUDGEMENT: coded YES because WHO AFRO's end-of-outbreak statement says the woman 'had exposure to the virus in Guinea' and 'her two children ... subsequently became infected'. However, WHO's 10 June 2016 situation report describes all three as having 'travelled from Macenta', and the children could have been exposed to their father in Guinea. If the children's infections are treated as imported, this episode flips to NO. Liberia declared over 9 June 2016.

excluded.reason: Fails the unit definition: the first laboratory-confirmed case (25 May 2014) was a funeral attendee in Sierra Leone; the funeral was of a traditional healer who had treated EVD patients from Guinea. No travelling index was ever laboratory-confirmed in Sierra Leone. SENSITIVITY CASE ONLY: outcome would be YES (massive local transmission).

The only reported travel-linked case was a probable (not laboratory-confirmed) case from Kailahun, Sierra Leone, who died in Foya and was buried in Sierra Leone; no lab-confirmed travelling index documented in WHO DONs.

uncertainties: Liberia March 2014: the 3 locally acquired lab-confirmed cases are inferred from WHO's statement that the 6 confirmed cases 'include 3 HCW'; WHO does not state where they were infected.

Liberia 2016: the YES rests on WHO AFRO's wording that the two children 'subsequently became infected'; WHO's 10 June 2016 situation report says all three 'travelled from Macenta', the children may have been exposed to their father in Guinea, and the arrival date conflicts (21 March per WHO AFRO vs 1 April per a 2018 J Infect Dis review).

Nigeria 2014: index confirmation date. WHO's spotlight says confirmation was announced 23 July; MMWR gives no date; WHO DON of 31 July still called the case 'probable' pending reference-lab testing. Arrival (20 July) is firm.
NYC 2014: arrival date. MMWR's 'returned to NYC nine days earlier' implies ~14 Oct; the commonly reported JFK arrival of 17 Oct was not checked against a primary source.
Italy 2015: arrival 7 May (WHO DON) vs 9 May (Bertoli et al. 2016).
Mali Kayes 2014: exact border-crossing date not published; 20 Oct is the Kayes admission date.
Uganda 2026: the index arrival date (8 May) is the EID 'date of emergence' (earliest crossing by any confirmed case), not explicitly the index; travel mode not stated in the sources reviewed.

Uganda 2026: imported vs local classification changed over time (Lancet ID modelling paper: 3 imported / 4 local of 7 as of 24 May; WHO final: 15 / 5 of 20; health-worker count revised 5 to 4). Outcome YES is robust; the count of 5 is WHO's final figure.
US surgeon 2026: positive date 17 May (DON605) vs lab confirmation received 20 May (DON603).
Uganda 2026 end: 28 July (end of local transmission, MoH) vs 27 August (formal end after the 42-day countdown, WHO/Africa CDC); ECDC says 25 August, which does not match WHO.

France 2026: 24 June is the WHO-notification and announcement date; the exact lab-result date is not stated. The French ministry press release could not be retrieved (automated access blocked), so French facts rest on WHO DONs 612-616 and ECDC.
Uganda Aug 2019: the MoH end-of-outbreak release is datelined 28 Oct 2019 but says 42 days since the last death (30 Aug), which would be ~11 Oct. Outcome unaffected.

Mali Bamako 2014 (sensitivity case): 6 confirmed + 1 probable local cases is derived by combining WHO 21 Nov 2014, the WHO spotlight ('seven additional cases'), the Mali total of 8 (MMWR/ECDC) and Hoenen 2015; no single primary source states 6 confirmed + 1 probable for the cluster.

Selection effects: the lab-confirmed-index rule removes importations recognised only through their secondary cases (Mali Bamako, Sierra Leone), which pushes the class toward NO. Including them pushes it toward YES, because importations that are never diagnosed and cause no transmission are never counted at all.

Heterogeneity: 4 of 13 indexes were returning responders/HCWs in high-income settings who self-monitored and reported early (all NO). Destination health-system preparedness also differs sharply between 2014 (pre-recognition Liberia) and 2019/2026 Uganda.

Completeness: the search covered WHO DONs, MMWR, EID, ECDC and PubMed for 2000-2026. Undocumented or unreported cross-border importations (especially land crossings in Central/East Africa) may be missing; no qualifying 2000-2013 episode was found.

Episode-boundary judgements: Mali Kayes and Mali Bamako are separate units (sequencing shows independent introductions and the Kayes chain produced no transmission); Uganda June and August 2019 are separate units (the June episode was declared over ~25 July); NYC is separate from Dallas.
Liberia 2016: the WHO Regional Office for Africa page cited for the outbreak's end now displays 12 June 2017; the event date recorded here (June 2016) is the event's, not the page's.
